title: ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF FRAMEWORK ACT ON SETTLING THE PAST FOR TRUTH AND RECONCILIATION
full_text:
Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe the matters mandated by the Framework Act on Settling the Past for Truth and Reconciliation and matters necessary for the enforcement thereof.

Article 1-2 (Guarantee of right of persons harmed to submit opinions) (1) Persons harmed and their surviving family members may submit to the Commission opinions on truth-finding, recovery from damage, restoration of honor, memorial projects, etc. under Article 3(1) of the Act, and the Commission shall guarantee their right to submit such opinions.
  (2) Where persons harmed and their surviving family members have difficulty submitting opinions under paragraph (1) due to illness, disability, old age, etc., the Commission may provide necessary accommodations as prescribed by the rules of the Commission.
  [This Article Added on Aug. 4, 2026]

Article 2 (Quota of public officials) (1) Under Article 16 of the Framework Act on Settling the Past for Truth and Reconciliation (hereinafter referred to as the "Act"), the authorized number of public officials to be assigned to the Secretariat of the Truth and Reconciliation Commission under Article 4 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Commission") shall be as specified in Appendix 1.
  (2) Among the staff allocation of the Committee pursuant to paragraph (1) and Appendix 1, 3 members (2 administrative officers and 1 assistant administrative officer) shall be recruited from public officials belonging to the Ministry of Education; 3 members (1 administrative officer and 2 administrative junior officers) from the Ministry of Unification; 8 members (1 prosecution investigation officer, 2 prosecution officers, 3 prosecution junior officers, and 2 assistant prosecution officers) from the Ministry of Justice; 8 members (1 officer, 2 administrative officers, 3 administrative junior officers, and 2 assistant administrative officers) from the Ministry of National Defense; 16 members (1 public official in general service belonging to the Senior Executive Service, 1 deputy director or officer, 1 officer, 1 officer or administrative officer, 6 administrative officers, facilities officers or senior archivist-researchers, 3 administrative junior officers, 1 administrative junior officer or computer junior officer, 1 assistant administrative officer, and 1 assistant administrative officer or archivist-researcher) from the Ministry of the Interior and Safety; 5 members (1 administrative officer, 2 administrative junior officers, and 2 assistant administrative officers) from the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs; 1 member (1 administrative junior officer) from the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism; 2 members (1 administrative officer, social welfare officer, or health officer, and 1 administrative junior officer, social welfare junior officer, or health junior officer) from the Ministry of Health and Welfare; 2 members (2 administrative junior officers) from the Ministry of Employment and Labor; 2 members (2 administrative junior officers) from the Ministry of Gender Equality and Family; 2 members (1 information officer or investigation officer, and 1 information junior officer or investigation junior officer) from the National Intelligence Service; 1 member (1 administrative officer) from the Ministry of Personnel Management; 1 member (1 administrative officer) from the Anti-Corruption and Civil Rights Commission; and 7 members (2 superintendents, 1 inspector, 3 assistant inspectors, and 1 senior police officer) from the National Police Agency. <Amended on Jul. 7, 2026>

Article 3 (Expert members) Where the Commission deems it necessary to efficiently support its business affairs and to conduct specialized investigation and research, it may appoint expert advisors and auxiliary personnel within the limits of the budget.

Article 4 (Education and training) (1) In order to promote truth-finding and reconciliation, the Commission may engage in exchanges and cooperation with domestic and foreign institutions having professional knowledge and experience or, if necessary, dispatch its members or staff members or relevant experts to receive education related to truth-finding and reconciliation or to collect materials. <Amended on Aug. 4, 2026>
  (2) In order to promote the psychological stability and mental recovery of its staff members in the course of performing investigative duties, the Commission may provide psychological counseling, operate healing programs, and conduct related education, as prescribed by the rules of the Commission. <Added on Aug. 4, 2026>

Article 5 (Allowances) Allowances, travel expenses, and other necessary expenses may be paid, within the limits of the budget, to members who are not public officials, expert witnesses, witnesses, and relevant experts attending meetings of the Commission or its advisory bodies; provided, that such payments shall not be made where a public official attends in direct connection with his or her official duties.

Article 5-2 (Composition and Operation of Deliberative Public Forum) (1) The Commission shall hold the forum for collecting opinions under Article 18(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Deliberative Public Forum") at least twice a year.
  (2) The Deliberative Public Forum shall consist of not less than 16 and not more than 24 members, including 1 chairperson, and the chairperson shall be elected by and from among its members.
  (3) The term of office of a member under paragraph (2) shall be 1 year, and the member may be reappointed only once.
  (4) Where necessary for collecting opinions, the chairperson of the Deliberative Public Forum may request the Commission to provide necessary cooperation, including the submission of relevant materials. In such cases, the Commission shall cooperate with such request unless there are special circumstances.
  (5) The chairperson of the Deliberative Public Forum shall submit in writing to the Commission, without delay, the opinions collected at the Deliberative Public Forum.
  (6) The Commission shall review the matters submitted under paragraph (5) and notify the chairperson of the Deliberative Public Forum of the results within 60 days from the date of receipt thereof; provided, where unavoidable circumstances exist, such as where additional verification of facts is necessary, the Commission may, by decision, extend such period by up to 30 days.
  (7) Where the Commission intends to extend the notification period pursuant to the proviso of paragraph (6), it shall notify the chairperson of the Deliberative Public Forum of the grounds for and period of the extension.
  (8) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) through (7), matters necessary for the composition and operation of the Deliberative Public Forum, procedures for recommending its members, and other related matters shall be prescribed by the rules of the Commission.
  [This Article Added on Aug. 4, 2026]

Article 6 (Scope of familial relationship) (1) "Persons in a familial relationship" in Article 22(1) of the Act means persons included within the scope of relatives under Article 777 of the Civil Act.
  (2) "Persons having special knowledge of facts" in Article 22(1) of the Act means a person who has experienced or witnessed a truth-finding case or a person who has directly heard such facts from a person who experienced or witnessed the case; provided, in the case of a person who has directly heard such facts from such person, it shall be limited to cases where the person who experienced or witnessed the case is identifiable, alive, and capable of being investigated.

Article 7 (Procedures and Methods for filing an application for truth-finding) (1) A person who intends to apply to the Commission for truth-finding under Article 23(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as an "applicant") shall prepare an application for truth-finding prescribed by the rules of the Commission (hereinafter referred to as an "application form") and submit it to the Commission or to the head of a local government or an overseas diplomatic mission.
  (2) The head of a local government or an overseas diplomatic mission who receives an application form under paragraph (1) shall immediately forward it to the Commission.
  (3) Where an application for truth-finding is made orally under the proviso to, with the exception of the subparagraphs, of Article 23(1) of the Act, the Commission or the head of a local government or an overseas diplomatic mission shall prepare a written record thereof.
  (4) Where an application form requires supplementation, the Commission may request the applicant to supplement it.
  (5) An applicant may withdraw an application in writing or orally until a decision of dismissal without prejudice under Article 24(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a "decision of dismissal without prejudice") or a decision to commence a truth-finding investigation under Article 25(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a "decision to commence an investigation") is made. In such cases, if the applicant withdraws the application orally, the Commission shall prepare a written record thereof.
  (6) To facilitate applications for truth-finding, the Commission may publicize the procedures and methods for filing such applications through newspapers, broadcasting, information and communications networks, or other means.
  (7) For the convenience of filing applications for truth-finding, the Commission shall provide information on the procedures and methods for filing applications in the languages of major countries of overseas adoption and may provide necessary support, including accepting applications prepared in foreign languages and providing interpretation during investigations. <Added on Aug. 4, 2026>
  (8) Where, in the course of investigating a case for which an application for truth-finding has been filed under Article 22(1) of the Act, the Commission additionally identifies a case falling under any subparagraph of Article 2(1) of the Act (excluding a serious human rights violation case subject to an ex officio investigation under Article 25(4) of the Act), it shall provide information on the procedures for filing an application for truth-finding to a person eligible to file such application with respect to the relevant case, as prescribed by the rules of the Commission. <Added on Aug. 4, 2026>

Article 8 (Transfer and notification of applications) If it is clear that the matters stated in an application fall under the jurisdiction of another agency, the Commission shall, without delay, transfer the application to the relevant agency and notify the applicant thereof.

Article 9 (Time limit for decisions to commence investigations) The Commission shall make a decision of dismissal without prejudice or a decision to commence a truth-finding investigation within 90 days from the date an application is received by the Commission, the date an oral application is made, or the date an application is forwarded by the head of a local government or the head of an overseas diplomatic mission; provided, if a preliminary investigation is conducted under Article 25(2) of the Act, the Commission may, by resolution, extend the period within a limit of 30 days.

Article 10 (Reapplication) (1) If an applicant whose application has been dismissed without prejudice files a new application after remedying the grounds for dismissal without prejudice, the Commission shall receive such application.
  (2) Articles 7 and 8 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the procedures and methods for reapplication and to the transfer and notification of applications.

Article 11 (Procedures and methods of investigation) (1) Measures under Article 26(1) of the Act shall be taken in writing.
  (2) The hearing of statements from a person subject to investigation or a person for reference under Article 26(1)2 of the Act shall be conducted at the office of the Commission, except in cases of an on-site investigation under Article 26(4) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as an "on-site investigation"); provided, if the Commission so resolves, such hearing may be conducted at a third location.
  (3) When conducting an on-site investigation, the Commission shall notify in advance the agency, facility, or organization referred to in the first sentence of Article 26(4) of the Act of the date, place, purpose, and other relevant matters.
  (4) The identification verifying the authority of a commissioner or a staff member of the Commission who conducts an on-site investigation under the latter part of Article 26(4) of the Act shall be as prescribed in the Form.
  (5) When the Commission deems it necessary in connection with a truth-finding investigation under Article 25 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a "truth-finding investigation"), it may hear the opinions of domestic or foreign experts, interested persons, or persons with relevant knowledge and experience by allowing relevant experts to participate in the truth-finding investigation, holding public hearings, or by other means.
  (6) If the Commission determines that a person subject to investigation, a person for reference, or relevant evidence or materials are located in a foreign country, it may request cooperation from the relevant country or relevant persons through diplomatic channels.
  (7) Where the Commission deems it necessary during an on-site investigation, it may, with the consent of landowners, etc., handle necessary matters such as disinterment under Articles 8 and 27 of the Act on Funeral Services.

Article 12 (Recording of statements) Where the Commission deems it necessary when hearing statements from a person subject to investigation or a person for reference under Article 26(1)2 of the Act, it may have its staff members record the contents of the statement or videotape the scene of the statement with the consent of the person making the statement.

Article 12-2 (Duties of unit dedicated to exhumation of remains) (1) The unit dedicated to the exhumation of remains under Article 27(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "dedicated unit") shall perform the following duties:
  1. Investigation of the location and exhumation of the remains of victims related to cases for which an investigation has been commenced under Article 25 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "remains of victims");
  2. Identification of the remains of victims and their surviving family members;
  3. Collection, preservation, and management of materials relating to the exhumation of the remains of victims;
  4. Publicity relating to the exhumation of the remains of victims;
  5. Other matters that the chairperson of the Commission deems necessary in connection with the investigation and exhumation of the remains of victims.
  (2) The head of the dedicated unit shall exercise general supervision and control over the duties of the dedicated unit under the direction of the chairperson of the Commission.
  (3) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) and (2), matters regarding the organization of the dedicated unit, the division of duties, and other related matters shall be prescribed by the rules of the Commission.
  [This Article Added on Aug. 4, 2026]

Article 12-3 (Investigation and exhumation of remains of victims) (1) A person who intends to enter upon land, public waters, or other such places of another person (hereinafter referred to as "land, etc.") to investigate and exhume the remains of victims pursuant to Article 27(2) of the Act shall carry an identification indicating his or her authority and present it to the owner, possessor, or manager of the land, etc., or other interested persons (hereinafter referred to as "owners, etc."). In such cases, the form of such identification shall be prescribed by the rules of the Commission.
  (2) No person shall, before sunrise or after sunset, enter upon a building site or land, etc. of another person enclosed by a wall or fence without the consent of the possessor thereof.
  (3) An investigation and exhumation plan prepared by the Commission under Article 27(3) of the Act shall include the following:
  1. The purpose of the investigation and exhumation;
  2. The area subject to the investigation and exhumation;
  3. A plan for making inquiries regarding the area subject to the investigation and exhumation;
  4. Grounds for believing that the remains of victims are buried in the area subject to the investigation and exhumation;
  5. The methods and period of the investigation and exhumation;
  6. Matters regarding control of and recordkeeping at the site of the investigation and exhumation;
  7. Matters regarding the budget for the investigation and exhumation.
  (4) Where the Commission intends to give notice of an investigation and exhumation plan under Article 27(3) of the Act, it shall do so by visiting and delivering the notice to owners, etc. or by serving it by mail no later than 7 days before commencing the investigation and exhumation of the remains of victims.
  (5) The Commission may delegate part of its duties relating to the investigation and exhumation of the remains of victims to the head of a local government pursuant to Article 45(2) of the Act.
  (6) Where necessary in connection with duties relating to the investigation and exhumation of the remains of victims, the Commission may request cooperation from the head of the competent local government or the chief of the competent police station. In such cases, the head of the competent local government or the chief of the competent police station shall cooperate with such request unless there are special circumstances.
  (7) The Commission may hold briefing sessions for residents of the relevant area to facilitate the performance of duties relating to the investigation and exhumation of the remains of victims.
  [This Article Added on Aug. 4, 2026]

Article 12-4 (Preservation of remains of victims) (1) The Commission shall take the following measures to preserve the remains exhumed under Article 27(5) of the Act:
  1. Notifying owners, etc. of the discovery of remains;
  2. Installing signs at the site where remains are exhumed;
  3. Taking protective measures to prevent changes in the condition of the site, such as flooding, freezing, collapse, or washout of the site, and periodically inspecting the site;
  4. Taking security measures to prevent damage to or theft of exhumed remains;
  5. Transferring exhumed remains to a facility for the placement of remains operated by the State or a local government.
  (2) The Commission may request the head of a relevant central administrative agency or the head of the competent local government to cooperate in taking the measures specified in the subparagraphs of paragraph (1).
  (3) The State may operate a facility for the placement of remains to preserve exhumed remains or carry out memorial projects to commemorate victims.
  (4) Where the State or a local government places remains transferred pursuant to paragraph (1)5 in a facility, it shall respect the dignity of the remains.
  [This Article Added on Aug. 4, 2026]

Article 12-5 (Standards and methods for identification) (1) Where the Commission takes measures for identification pursuant to Article 27(6) of the Act, it shall comprehensively consider the following methods:
  1. Comparison and analysis of personal effects exhumed together with the remains of victims;
  2. Analysis of investigation materials for truth-finding for each case and related records;
  3. Comparison of testimony from informants, surviving family members, residents of the area where the remains of victims were exhumed, and other relevant persons;
  4. Forensic anthropological analysis to determine identity, time of death, cause of death, and other relevant facts;
  5. Genetic analysis, including genetic testing and comparison;
  6. Other scientifically proven methods of analysis for identification.
  (2) The Commission may request the National Forensic Service or other relevant institutions to take measures for identification or conduct genetic testing under Article 27(6) of the Act.
  [This Article Added on Aug. 4, 2026]

Article 12-6 (Procedures for compensation for loss) (1) A person who intends to receive compensation for loss pursuant to Article 27(7) of the Act shall submit to the Commission a claim form prescribed by the rules of the Commission, along with documents evidencing the loss.
  (2) Where documents submitted pursuant to paragraph (1) are deficient or where it is necessary to verify facts or for other purposes, the Commission may require supplementation thereof or the submission of additional materials.
  (3) Upon receipt of a claim form under paragraph (1), the Commission shall investigate the relevant facts and, after deliberation, determine whether to provide compensation and the amount thereof.
  (4) The Commission shall, within 10 days from the date of a determination under paragraph (3), notify the claimant, using a notice prescribed by the rules of the Commission, of whether compensation is to be provided and the details thereof.
  (5) Where the Commission determines to provide compensation, it shall pay the compensation within 1 month from the date on which it notifies the claimant of the determination pursuant to paragraph (4).
  (6) A person who objects to a determination under paragraph (3) shall, within 30 days from the date on which the person is served with the notice under paragraph (4), submit to the Commission a written objection prescribed by the rules of the Commission, along with documents evidencing the grounds for the objection.
  (7) Upon receipt of a written objection under paragraph (6), the Commission shall investigate the relevant facts and, after deliberation, redetermine whether to provide compensation and the amount thereof. In such cases, paragraphs (4) and (5) shall apply mutatis mutandis to notification of the determination and the method of payment of compensation, respectively.
  [This Article Added on Aug. 4, 2026]

Article 13 (Notification of decisions and procedures for filing objections) (1) Notification of a decision under Article 38(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "notification of a decision") shall be made in writing within 1 week from the date the decision is made.
  (2) A person who intends to file an objection pursuant to Article 38(4) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as an "objector") shall submit to the Commission an objection form prescribed by the rules of the Commission stating the following matters. In such cases, relevant documents or materials proving the grounds for the objection shall be attached:
  1. The name and address of the person filing the objection;
  2. The date of receipt of notification of a decision;
  3. The matters notified or the contents of the decision;
  4. Grounds for filing an objection.
  (3) When the Commission finds that supplementation is required with respect to an objection filed under paragraph (2), it shall request supplementation by written notice stating the following matters; in such cases, the period for supplementation shall not be included in the period for notifying the results of the objection under Article 38(5) of the Act:
  1. The matters requiring supplementation;
  2. The reasons for requesting supplementation;
  3. The period for supplementation;
  4. Other matters the Commission deems necessary.

Article 13-2 (Scope and methods of disclosure of decisions) (1) Where the Commission discloses the contents of a decision under the main clause of Article 39 of the Act, the disclosure shall include the following:
  1. The type of decision;
  2. The name of the case;
  3. The reasons for decision;
  4. In the case of a decision of truth-finding under Article 36 of the Act, matters recommended pursuant to Article 43(4) of the Act in connection with the relevant case.
  (2) Where the Commission discloses the contents of a decision pursuant to the main clause of Article 39 of the Act, it need not disclose information that constitutes personal information under subparagraph 1 of Article 2 of the Personal Information Protection Act and is deemed likely to infringe on the privacy or freedom of an individual if disclosed.
  (3) Where the Commission discloses the contents of a decision pursuant to the main clause of Article 39 of the Act, it may do so by posting them on the website of the Commission.
  (4) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) through (3), matters regarding the methods and procedures for disclosure of decisions and other related matters shall be prescribed by the rules of the Commission.
  [This Article Added on Aug. 4, 2026]

Article 14 (Consultation on dispatch of public officials) If the chairperson of the Commission intends to request the dispatch of a public official belonging to a State agency or a local government to the Commission under Article 40(1) of the Act, the chairperson shall have a prior consultation with the head of such state organ or local government.

Article 15 (Protection of informants) When the Commission deems that a person who has participated in a truth-finding investigation or a person who has discovered or submitted materials necessary for truth-finding is under, or is likely to be under, a threat to his or her life or body from another person, the Commission may request the relevant agency to provide personal protection; provided, the agency receiving such request from the Commission shall comply with it without delay.

Article 16 (Support from State agencies) (1) Relevant agencies such as State agencies and local governments shall, where requested by the Commission under Article 45(1) of the Act, provide conveniences such as the provision of venues and may support the personnel necessary for the performance of the duties of the Commission.
  (2) The Commission may establish and operate a working-level consultative council to facilitate cooperation with relevant agencies, including State agencies and local governments. <Amended on Aug. 4, 2026>
  (3) The Commission may jointly perform the following duties with the heads of relevant agencies, including State agencies and local governments, pursuant to Article 45(2) of the Act: <Amended on Aug. 4, 2026>
  1. Receipt of applications;
  2. Publicizing the procedures and methods for filing applications for truth-finding under Article 7(6);
  3. Investigation of the factual background.
  4. Investigation of the human rights conditions of surviving persons harmed and surviving family members.
  (4) Matters necessary for the procedures and methods for performing the duties under paragraphs (2) and (3) shall be determined by the chairperson of the Commission following a resolution of the Commission after hearing the opinions of relevant agencies, including State agencies and local governments. <Amended on Aug. 4, 2026>
  (5) The Commission may provide relevant agencies with funds necessary for performing duties jointly with relevant agencies, including State agencies and local governments, pursuant to paragraph (3). <Amended on Aug. 4, 2026>
  [Title Amended on Aug. 4, 2026]

Article 17 (Joint performance of business affairs) Pursuant to Article 45(2) of the Act, the Commission may jointly perform part of the truth-finding activities regarding the matters referred to in Article 2(1)1 and 2 with relevant specialized institutions or academic or research organizations.

Article 18 (Consultation and coordination of truth-finding activities) The Commission may consult and coordinate with State agencies that have established special bodies and the relevant special bodies on the following matters under Article 45(3) of the Act.
  1. Matters regarding the selection of persons subject to investigation;
  2. Matters regarding the coordination of overlapping investigations into a case, which are undertaken by the Commission and a special body;
  3. Where further investigations or verification procedures are required to address social issues arising from a case into which the Commission or a special body has concluded or is currently conducting investigations, matters regarding the methods and procedures therefor;
  4. Matters regarding preliminary investigations;
  5. Matters regarding requests for relevant materials;
  6. Matters regarding the disclosure of investigation findings;
  7. Matters regarding follow-up measures to achieve reconciliation, such as by repairing harm or restoring honor, following the establishment of the truth.

Article 19 (Support for establishment of Past Affairs Research Foundation) (1) The Commission may support the establishment and projects of the Past Affairs Research Foundation under Article 55 of the Act.
  (2) Detailed matters regarding the support under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by the rules of the Commission.

Article 19-2 (Follow-up measures under special cases concerning extinctive prescription for claims for damages) (1) The Commission may provide information or conduct publicity activities to ensure that the public, persons related to cases subject to truth-finding, and other relevant persons are informed of the purpose and details of Article 61 of the Act and Article 5 of the Addenda to the wholly amended Framework Act on Settling the Past for Truth and Reconciliation (Act No. 21330).
  (2) The timing and methods of providing information and conducting publicity activities under paragraph (1) and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by the rules of the Commission.
  [This Article Added on Aug. 4, 2026]

Article 20 (Criteria for imposition of administrative fines) The criteria for the imposition of administrative fines under Article 66(1) and (2) of the Act shall be as specified in Appendix 2.

Article 21 (Detailed operating rules) Detailed matters necessary for the enforcement of this Decree shall be determined by the chairperson of the Commission upon resolution of the Commission.

Article 22 (Period of existence of the Secretariat) The secretariat shall continue to exist for three more months after the Commission completes its operation.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 36123, Feb. 25, 2026>
Article 1 (Enforcement date)
This Decree shall enter into force on February 26, 2026.
Article 2 (Transitional measures concerning public officials affiliated with Commission upon expiration of period of existence of Secretariat)
If there are public officials (excluding public officials in extraordinary civil service) affiliated with the Commission at the time the period of existence of the Secretariat of the Commission expires under the amended provisions of Article 22, it shall be deemed that the central administrative agency to which the relevant public officials originally belong has a separate quota corresponding to the current number of such public officials.
Article 3 Omitted.
